question: What do the stone-carved wheels of the Konark Sun Temple symbolically depict?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Measurement of time cycles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **stone-carved wheels** of the **Konark Sun Temple** are iconic structures that symbolically depict the **measurement of time cycles**. These wheels are not merely decorative but have a significant astronomical and functional value.
 
• Each of the wheels represents a **sun dial**, functioning as a tool to measure time. The intricate carvings and divisions on the wheels align with the hours, minutes, and seconds of the day. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• The design of the wheels reflects the ancient Indian understanding of **astronomy** and the passage of time through celestial movements. These wheels are integral to the temple's association with the **Sun God, Surya**, who symbolizes the cyclic nature of time. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• The wheels consist of **24 spokes**, symbolizing the 24 hours of a day. The divisions further denote smaller units of time, emphasizing the advanced knowledge of timekeeping possessed by the architects of the temple.
 
• The positioning and orientation of the wheels are aligned with the **movement of the sun**, showcasing the synchronization between architecture and astronomy. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• While the wheels primarily depict the measurement of time cycles, they also signify the cyclic nature of life and time, a recurring theme in Indian philosophy.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Measurement of time cycles.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Konark Sun Temple:**

 
 
• The **Konark Sun Temple**, located in **Odisha, India**, was built in the **13th century** by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.
 
• The temple is dedicated to the **Sun God, Surya**, and is designed in the shape of a colossal chariot with **12 pairs of intricately carved wheels** and seven horses.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Wheels:**
 
 
• The wheels are not just artistic elements but serve as **functional sundials**. By observing the shadow cast by the central axle of the wheels, one can determine the time of the day.
 
• The **24 spokes** represent the hours of a day, and the carvings on the wheels illustrate the **cyclic nature of time** in Indian cosmology.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Brilliance:**
 
 
• The positioning of the wheels aligns with the **movement of the sun**, reflecting the advanced astronomical knowledge of the builders.
 
• The temple itself is a masterpiece of **Kalinga architecture**, showcasing intricate carvings, sculptures, and engineering marvels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**

 
 
• The **Konark Sun Temple** was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1984** due to its cultural and architectural significance.
 
• It is considered one of the finest examples of **Indian temple architecture** and is a major tourist attraction.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Challenges:**
 
 
• The temple has suffered damage over the centuries due to **natural calamities**, invasions, and lack of maintenance.
 
• Efforts are being made by the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** to restore and preserve this historical monument.
